title: A data-driven framework for identifying innovation pathways in rice abiotic stress research
desc: Research on abiotic stress-related traits in rice—particularly salt tolerance, drought tolerance, and cadmium accumulation—is important for understanding environmental constraints on crop performance and supporting trait improvement. However, scientific innovation in this field still relies heavily on expert experience, and existing research data remain fragmented and dispersed across pathways, making it difficult to systematically integrate experimental technologies, biological entities, environmental factors, and phenotypic traits into traceable innovation pathways. To address this gap, this study develops a data-driven methodological framework that integrates multi-source data fusion, knowledge-base enhancement, multilayer heterogeneous-network construction, multidimensional innovation-feature measurement, and innovation-pathway identification. A curated literature dataset was first constructed by integrating full-text research articles with domain knowledge bases. A knowledge-base-enhanced entity–relation extraction model (KB-EREM), combining Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (BERT) with Lightweight Retrieval-Augmented Generation (LightRAG) was subsequently developed. A technology-data heterogeneous network was then built, comprising nine categories of scientific data and technical entities together with eight types of association relationships. On this basis, an innovation-feature measurement indicator system was established across five dimensions—data-drivenness, interdisciplinarity, connectivity, frontier orientation, and breakthrough potential—and the entropy-weighted Technique for Order Preference by Similarity to Ideal Solution (TOPSIS) method was employed to quantify innovation characteristics along scientific research chains. An iterative depth-first search (DFS) algorithm was further used to identify innovation pathways within the heterogeneous network, thereby identifying potential innovation pathways in rice abiotic-stress research. The framework extracted 10,409 entity instances and 13,034 relation instances, with F1-scores of 87.58% for entity extraction and 75.03% for relation extraction. Empirical results show that innovation pathways in rice abiotic-stress research exhibit a characteristic “technological support → gene-related association → phenotypic realisation” structure, and the associations among molecular breeding technologies, environmental factors, and target traits occupy central positions in the network. Using salt-tolerance research as an example, pathways associated with SHMT3, HOG1, and OsVTC1-3 display high innovation-feature values, identifying these genes as literature-derived, computationally prioritised candidates associated with rice salt tolerance, whose biological roles require further experimental validation. The findings demonstrate that the proposed method effectively identifies traceable innovation pathways in rice abiotic-stress research, providing methodological support for literature-based candidate prioritisation, research-pathway tracing, and hypothesis generation in data-intensive crop research.

title: A novel hybrid fuzzy membership function-based feature transformation for cardiovascular disease prediction
desc: Cardiovascular disease portrays a critical health issue due to its huge numbers of morbidity and mortality rate. Stable, accurate prediction and diagnosis are important for early intervention, monitoring, and treatment. The area of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Internet of Medical Things (IoMT) significantly enhanced the healthcare sector, providing early detection of diseases, diagnosis, monitoring, and personalized care. Despite the advancement in AI-based diagnosis system existing methods often struggle with handling uncertainty, complexity, discreteness in datasets which leads to model overfitting, poses a significant challenge to develop a generalized model. This study proposes a novel hybrid fuzzy membership function-based feature transformation technique. The proposed technique combines gaussian function to capture localized precision in high-confidence region and sigmoid functions ensure smooth transition in area with greater certainty. Subsequently, the proposed hybrid fuzzy membership function (F-MF) integrated with gradient boosting decision tree (GBDT) and bagging Fuzzy-GBDT for heart disease prediction. The proposed approaches reduce overfitting, adapt to complex, nonlinear decision boundaries and improve predictability of individual features, resulting in improved model generalization and overall prediction performance. The validation of the proposed methodology is carried out on two publicly available benchmark datasets: (1) UCI Heart Disease dataset and (2) a publicly available Kaggle version of the Framingham dataset for cardiovascular risk prediction. The proposed model on Dataset 1 achieved accuracy of 98%, precision of 98%, recall of 98%, F1 score of 99% and AU-ROC (Area Under- Receiver Operating Characteristics) score 0.99. The model achieved an accuracy of 84.23%, precision of 88.86%, recall of 70.49%, F1 score of 78.62% and AU-ROC of 0.91 on Dataset 2. Furthermore, 10-fold cross-validation confirms the model’s generalizability, with minimum variance in performance across all folds. These results highlight the potential of hybrid fuzzy membership functions with GBDT models for reliable, interpretable CVD prediction subject to further external and clinical validation.
